title: Actors Protect Mutable State
hints: An `actor` protects its mutable state by running one call at a time.
Deposit from separate child tasks in a task group, each calling `await account.deposit(amount)`.
`actor Account { private var balance = 0; func deposit(_ a: Int) { balance += a }; var current: Int { balance } }`.
jsBridge: An `actor` serialises access to its state, like a JS object that only ever runs on one event loop, but in a multithreaded world. Every outside call is `await`ed, and the compiler forbids unsynchronised access.

compass.q: Why don't JS objects need actors (single-threaded event loop)? What changes once Web Workers share memory (`SharedArrayBuffer`)?
Actor **reentrancy**: during an `await` inside an actor method, other calls can run. How can that break an invariant?
Java `synchronized` vs Swift `actor`: what does each protect, and which can deadlock?
Would you make an image cache an actor? What about a view model (`@MainActor` instead)?
